verdict.headline: Chip stocks fall an eighth straight day and pull the S&P 500 below the line it held all week
verdict.label: Close: S&P 500 7,659.44 (-1.09%), seven points below 7,666.45; Nasdaq 26,140.03 (-2.14%, week -4.5%); Dow 52,002.41 (-0.34%); Russell 2000 -1.72%; chips -3.8%, eighth straight fall; VIX ~20; 10Y ~5.085%; Brent $109.86 (+3.7%); BTC $81,494.
verdict.rationale_short: The chip index fell 3.8% for an eighth straight day, its longest losing run since 2008 and 11.4% on the week, and CoreWeave lost about 12% as questions about debt-funded AI buildouts returned a day after Jensen Huang's defense. The S&P 500 fell 1.09% to 7,659.44, seven points below 7,666.45, the level the last two reports named as the sign of selling spreading beyond AI. Rates were not the cause: the two-year fell about 3 basis points and FedWatch put an October hold above 80%. The break was narrow. The Dow lost only 0.34% as energy rose with Brent at $109.86, while the Russell 2000 fell 1.72%, so the selling reached small caps but not the whole market. This morning's read that the selling is about AI financing rather than rates held up. A close back above 7,666.45 would point to an options-expiry overshoot; the Dow joining the decline would confirm broader selling. Meta and Tesla report Wednesday.
verdict.lede_short: Chip stocks fell for an eighth straight day, the longest run since 2008, and pulled the S&P 500 1.1% lower to 7,659, just under the level it had held all week. Rates were not the cause: near-term Fed hike odds fell. The Dow lost only 0.3% as oil neared $110, so the selling reached small caps but not the whole market. A close back above 7,666 would make Friday look like an options-expiry overshoot.

supporting_data.label: The chip index fell 3.8% for an eighth straight day and 11.4% on the week, its worst week since April 2025, with CoreWeave down about 12% — questions about debt-funded AI buildouts undid Thursday's rebound in one session.
The S&P 500 fell 1.1% to 7,659.44 and the Nasdaq 2.1%, while the Dow lost only 0.3% and rose 0.7% on the week — a 5-point weekly gap between the Nasdaq and the Dow measures the move out of tech.
The two-year fell more than 3 basis points to 4.715% and FedWatch put an October hold above 80% — near-term rate risk eased and chips fell anyway, so rates are not what is driving the selling.
Brent touched $110 for the first time since May and settled up 3.7% at $109.86 as Iran stepped up attacks near Hormuz — oil adds a second cost pressure on top of September's hot PPI.
The VIX rose about 21% to just above 20 after topping 22 intraday, its first time there in four months — options buyers paid for protection they declined to buy on Thursday.

About 70 S&P 500 companies report next week, with Tesla and Meta on Wednesday, after 85% of the first 46 beat estimates — Meta's spending plans are the first direct read on AI demand since the chip selling began.

watchlist_mentions.note: Fell 1.17% to $214.70 while Micron fell 5.6% and Intel 5.8% — again the smallest decline among the major chip names.
Fell about 12% and is down 25% on the week, undoing Thursday's rebound after Huang's defense in one session.
Closed down 2.13% at $354.72 after trading up about 2.4% before the open on the Roadster reveal; reports Wednesday October 21.
Fell 7.2% to $186.03, the largest drop among the large AI software names.
Fell 3.72% to $709.33 ahead of Wednesday's results, where capital spending plans are the read on AI demand.
Little changed near $81,500, about $1,200 above the $80,320 low; Strategy fell nearly 10% on the MSCI index rule change.

trade_setups.thesis: The index closed seven points below 7,666.45 on options-expiry day, with the Dow down only 0.34% and the Russell 2000 down 1.72%; whether the break holds decides whether the selling has spread beyond AI hardware.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back above 7,666.45 would point to an expiry overshoot; a second close below with the Dow down more than 1% would confirm broader selling

trade_setups.thesis: Brent settled at $109.86 after touching $110 for the first time since May, with Hormuz flows about 30% below pre-war levels and the diesel-first reserve release ending around October 22.
trade_setups.invalidation: A settle above $110 as the release tapers would strengthen the December hike case; a return toward $104.7 would ease it

trade_setups.asset: Meta and the AI demand read
trade_setups.thesis: Meta reports Wednesday after an 11.4% weekly fall in chips; its capital spending guidance is the first direct read from a large AI buyer since the selling began.
trade_setups.entry: Meta $709.33 close; chip index eight straight declines
trade_setups.invalidation: Spending held or raised would argue against the slowdown chip prices imply; a cut would support it
